instruction: GUI-only requirement: Complete the task entirely in the launched Bonsai/Blender graphical user interface. Do not open Terminal or a shell; do not use the Blender Python console, Text editor scripts, Python, IfcOpenShell, shell commands, or any helper script/macro to directly generate or edit the deliverable files. Use only Bonsai/Blender native GUI tools, panels, menus, dialogs, and built-in save/export commands. Open the provided init.ifc wall shell in Bonsai. Add hosted door and window openings, then save the completed IFC4 model as /home/user/Desktop/result.ifc using Bonsai's graphical save/export controls. The result should contain one project, one building storey, four walls, one slab, two doors, three windows, five opening elements, five void relationships, and five fill relationships. Do not include IfcBuildingElementProxy or IfcFurnishingElement objects. Every door and window must fill exactly one opening, and each of those openings must void an IfcWall. Host one door in Wall-S, one door in Wall-N, two windows in Wall-N, and one window in Wall-E. Do not create a CSV schedule or separate report file; the hosted opening relationships must be represented directly in result.ifc. Other non-required IFC metadata may vary as long as the saved model satisfies these stated GUI-created IFC requirements.
